column1: # 1. He lumi hou ko ka hale = The new room of the house
# 2. Ua nui ko Kimo hauʻoli i ka lohe ʻana e pili ana i ka pēpē hou. = Kimo was so happy when he heard about the new baby.
# 3. ʻO Kimo ke keiki hoʻokahi o ka ʻohana Komohale, a kokoke e piha ʻelima makahiki iā ia i kēia wā. = Kimo is the only child in the Komohale family, and he is almost five years old now.

# 4. Akā naʻe, i nehinei nō i haʻi mai ai kona māmā a me kona pāpā iā ia e loaʻa ana he pēpē hou ma ka ʻohana. = But just yesterday his mother and father told him that their family is going to have a new baby.
# 5. Hoʻokahi wale nō naʻe pilikia o ka ʻohana Komohale. = The Komohale family, however, has one problem.
# 6. Ua liʻiliʻi loa ko lākou hale, a makemake lākou e pākuʻi i lumi moe hou no ka pēpē. = Their house is very small and they want to add on a new bedroom for the baby.
# 7. "E Pāpā, na wai e kūkulu ana i ka lumi moe hou?" i nīnau ai ʻo Kimo. = "Papa, who is going to build the new bedroom?" asked Kimo.
# 8. "E kelepona wau iā ʻAnakala Kālai i kēia ahiahi. = "I'll phone Uncle Kālai this evening.
# 9. Hiki paha iā ia ke kōkua iā kākou, no ka mea, he kamanā maikaʻi loa ʻo ia." = Maybe he can help us, because he's a very good carpenter."
# 10. "He aha ka hana a ke kamanā?" i nīnau ai ʻo Kimo. = "What does a carpenter do?" asked Kimo.
# 11. "He kanaka kūkulu hale ʻo ia," i pane aku ai ko Kimo pāpā. = "He's a person who builds houses," answered Kimo's father.
# 12. "A kokoke e paʻa ka hale āna e kūkulu nei." = And Uncle Kālai is almost done with the house he is building."
# 13. Ua kāhea ko Kimo pāpā iā ʻAnakala Kālai, a ʻae maila ʻo ia e kōkua mai iā lākou. = Kimo's father called Uncle Kālai, and he agreed to help them.

# 14. No laila, ua hele ʻo Kimo me kona pāpā i ka hale kūʻai papa lāʻau e ʻoka aku ai i nā papa lāʻau a me nā kui no ke kūkulu ʻana i ka lumi hou. = So Kimo and his father went to the lumber store to order the lumber and nails to build the new room.
# 15. I ia Poʻaono aʻe, ua ala ʻo Kimo i ke kakahiaka nui no ka nui o kona pīhoihoi. = The next Saturday, Kimo woke up early in the morning because he was so excited.
# 16. I ka hōʻea ʻana mai o ʻAnakala Kālai, hea akula ʻo Kimo "Aloha e ʻAnakala, naʻu ʻoe e kōkua aku!" = When Uncle Kālai arrived, Kimo called out, "Hi, Uncle, I'm going to help you!"
# 17. "ʻAe, hiki nō!" i pane aku ai ʻo ʻAnakala. = "Okay!" answered Uncle.
# 18. "E kiʻi mua ʻoe i kaʻu lula." = "First go get my tape measure."
# 19. Ua hauʻoli ʻo Kimo i ke kiʻi ʻana i nā pono hana a ʻAnakala i makemake ai. = Kimo was happy to get the tools that Uncle wanted.
# 20. Hoihoi ʻo ia i ko lākou hoʻohana ʻia ʻana. = He was interested in how they were used.

# 21. Ke kāhea ʻo ʻAnakala Kālai, "E Kimo, e lawe mai ʻoe i ka hāmale," kiʻi koke aku ʻo Kimo i ka hāmale, a nānā akula ʻo ia i kā ʻAnakala hili ʻana i ke kui. = When Uncle Kālai called, "Kimo, bring me the hammer," Kimo quickly fetched the hammer, and he watched Uncle pound the nail.
# 22. Kiʻi ʻo ia i ka pahiolo, a nānā i ke olo ʻana i ka lāʻau. = He fetched the saw and watched him saw the wood.
# 23. Kiʻi ʻo ia i ke koʻikahi, a nānā i ke kahi ʻana i ka papa lāʻau. = He fetched the planer and watched him plane the boards.
# 24. A kiʻi ʻo ia i ke ana ʻiliwai, a nānā i ke ana ʻana i ka ʻiliwai o ka paepae pukaaniani. = He fetched the level and watched him check the level of the windowsill.
# 25. A paʻa ka lumi moe hou, mahalo akula ʻo Kimo i nā hana a ke kamanā. = When the new bedroom was finished, Kimo admired the carpenter's handiwork.
# 26. Ua ʻike ʻo ia e mahalo pū ana ka pēpē hou i kona lumi hou. = And he knew that the new baby would also appreciate the new room.
